mechanism_narrative: A persistently low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS <= 0.1%) indicates an accommodative monetary policy stance, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when FEDFUNDS <= 0.1% is negative or not significantly positive (p>0.05 in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening monetary cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, the 5-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous expansion in the labor force (PAYEMS rising) and decline in unemployment (UNRATE falling) signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative in more than 40% of periods where PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, rising housing starts (HOUST) and robust GDP growth (GDPC1) indicate strong underlying demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In the late-cycle expansion regime, the average 20-day forward return when HOUST and GDPC1 are above their 12-month moving averages is negative.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) indicates expanding manufacturing output, which correlates with stronger corporate profits and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 20-day forward return when INDPRO increases is negative or not significantly positive (p>0.05 in a one-sample t-test against zero).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPI increase exceeding 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, which prompts central bank tightening and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL y/y > 2.5%, the 20-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Strong consumer demand, as indicated by high retail sales (RSAFS), leads to elevated corporate revenues and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The average 60-day forward return when RSAFS is above its 12-month moving average is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in industrial production below 0.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where INDPRO monthly change < 0.5%, the 5-day forward return is positive in more than 40% of cases.
